rebuttal_items.question: How does the dispatch decision boundary adapt when node failure occurs mid-execution?
rebuttal_items.author_response: We thank Reviewer 1 for this insightful observation. In Section III-C, we have clarified the dynamic decision boundary behavior under node degradation. Specifically, when a node experiences latency spikes, the dispatch heuristic shifts subsequent tasks to alternate processors within O(log |N|) time.
rebuttal_items.manuscript_action: Clarified dynamic fault mitigation in Section III-C.

rebuttal_items.question: Could the authors confirm whether makespan improvements persist across skewed workload traces?
rebuttal_items.author_response: We appreciate Reviewer 2's feedback regarding workload distribution sensitivity. Across 10 randomized evaluation seeds recorded in paper/results.csv, Adaptive-DynaSched consistently outperforms Round-Robin by 22.41% in makespan (482.15s vs. 621.40s, p < 10^-6, Cohen's d = 2.45), even under skewed arrivals.
rebuttal_items.manuscript_action: Referenced 10-seed empirical ledger verification in Section IV-B.

rebuttal_items.question: Are all vector graphics prepared to scale cleanly to 3.5-inch column constraints without line weight loss?
rebuttal_items.author_response: We thank Reviewer 3 for highlighting graphical presentation clarity. All architectural and data flow diagrams have been rendered as 600 DPI vector PDFs and 300+ DPI PNGs conforming to IEEE 3.5-inch column guidelines.
rebuttal_items.manuscript_action: Enhanced vector graphic scaling and label typography in Section V.
